note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: acute onset breathlessness with right-sided pleuritic back pain and haemoptysis.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Symptoms began today (acute).
  - Cough with blood on two occasions today.
  - Subjective fever/feeling warm today (temperature not measured with thermometer).
  - Two weeks of increasing fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance preceding acute symptoms.
- Associated symptoms/triggers:
  - Pain on deep inspiration, localized to right side of back.
  - Subjective awareness of heart beating more than usual.
  - No recent long-haul travel reported.
  - No prior history of venous thromboembolism; no family history of clots reported.
- Context/other relevant details:
  - Non-smoker, works a desk job, lives alone in a flat, has a cat.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
- Medications: Methotrexate — dose/route/frequency not documented. Last dose taken this morning.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Other diagnoses/hospitalizations: Patient reports no other illnesses.

Physical Examination:
- Remote/limited exam performed during video consultation:
  - Radial pulse counted by patient: approximately 66–74 beats per minute (calculated by clinician from patient counting).
  - Capillary refill/circulation: described as good on video (no delayed refill reported).
  - Oropharyngeal view: visualized remotely; clinician reported no abnormality on inspection.
  - Neck palpation (patient self-exam): no enlarged glands noticed.
  - General: clinician noted patient did not appear acutely unstable based on limited remote assessment.
- Relevant negatives: No documented throat swelling; no documented fever measured with thermometer; no documented blood pressure, respiratory rate, or oxygen saturation.

Impression:
- Suspected chest infection/possible pneumonia presenting with pleuritic right-sided chest pain and haemoptysis — requires face-to-face assessment to confirm and exclude other causes.

Management Plan:
- Immediate:
  - Arrange urgent face-to-face review today with clinician to:
    - Auscultate chest with stethoscope.
    - Measure vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
    - Reassess haemoptysis and pleuritic pain.
  - No antibiotics prescribed remotely at this time; antibiotics may be started after in-person assessment if indicated.
- Possible next interventions after face-to-face assessment:
  - Chest X-ray if clinical examination suggests pneumonia or if symptoms do not resolve.
  - Further investigations/treatment based on in-person findings.
- Administrative:
  - Patient to ring support team (phone number to be left in notes) to book same-day face-to-face GP appointment.

Patient Summary:
- A 45-year-old patient with SLE on methotrexate presented with acute onset right-sided pleuritic back pain, cough with haemoptysis (two episodes), subjective fever, and two weeks of fatigue. The presentation is most consistent with a chest infection; a same-day face-to-face assessment is planned to examine the chest, obtain vital signs, consider antibiotics, and determine need for imaging.

Key Takeaways:
- Be seen in person today for chest auscultation and vitals — this is necessary before prescribing antibiotics.
- If examination suggests pneumonia or if symptoms persist/worsen, a chest X-ray and further investigations may be required.
- Contact the support team to arrange the face-to-face GP appointment (number to be left in notes).

Next Steps:
- Patient to be booked for urgent face-to-face GP review today (support team to arrange).
- In-person clinician to perform chest auscultation, measure baseline observations (BP, HR, temp, RR, SpO2), and decide on antibiotic therapy.
- Consider chest radiograph if clinical findings or clinical course warrant.
